key_insight: K-Bench provides a clinically calibrated way to test whether LLMs can handle multi-turn mental health conversations safely, especially when risk escalates. It benchmarks many models side-by-side on realistic vignettes covering suicide, self-harm, domestic violence, substance misuse, and no-risk cases.
problem_solved: Current evaluations do not adequately capture how LLMs behave in evolving, high-risk mental health conversations. This paper addresses the need for a protected, clinician-informed benchmark that can assess safety and response quality in realistic multi-turn scenarios.
method: Built K-Bench as a protected benchmark with 200 multi-turn mental health vignettes.
Clinically calibrated the scenarios to cover suicide, self-harm, domestic violence, substance misuse, and no-risk presentations.
Evaluated 125 model configurations across 33 base models from 14 providers to compare safety behavior under risk.
Used synthetic patient interactions to simulate realistic, evolving conversations.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, K-Bench offers a more realistic safety evaluation framework for deploying LLMs in mental health settings. It helps identify which models are more robust in high-stakes conversations and where they may fail, supporting safer model selection and improvement.

paper_title: K-Bench: a clinically calibrated benchmark for evaluating large language models in high-risk mental health conversations
paper_authors: Laura M. Vowels, Matthew J. Vowels, Shivali Sharma, Apoorv Jha, Rehnuma Choudhury
